;;;; Flags, an extension, an active filter, and a child that keeps only
;;;; what is shared. Every trap in this family, composed.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(defmacro deftool (var &key name)
  `(defvar ,var (make-tool :name (or ,name (string-downcase (symbol-name ',var))))))

(deftool read-tool :name "read")
(deftool edit-tool :name "edit")
(deftool find-tool :name "search")
(deftool write-tool :name "write")
(deftool bash-tool :name "bash")

(register read-tool)
(register edit-tool)
(register find-tool)

(defun enable-shell ()
  ;; Nothing calls this.
  (register bash-tool))

(defparameter +unshared+ '("audit-log")
  "Lead-only tools; a child never receives them.")

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-lead-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  (let ((active '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")))
    (list :tools (remove-if-not (lambda (tool)
                                  (member (tool-name tool) active :test #'string=))
                                *registry*))))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (list :tools (remove-if (lambda (tool)
                            (member (tool-name tool) +unshared+ :test #'string=))
                          (getf parent :tools))))

is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be
overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:
`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

ascending by string<. Grading runs against a pristine copy of these files
plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

The harness: config.lisp defines *flags* = '(:audit), flag-enabled-p. harness.lisp loads extension.lisp inside make-lead-agent. extension.lisp registers "audit-log" (since :audit flag enabled) and "trace" is not registered (flag not enabled).

But note: make-lead-agent loads extension.lisp. The load happens each time make-lead-agent is called. Registration: register adds to *registry*, removing existing with same name. So registry after: read-tool ("read"), edit-tool ("edit"), find-tool ("search"), plus audit-log from extension. write-tool, bash-tool defined but not registered (bash only registered if enable-shell called, which nothing calls).

Then active = '("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate"). remove-if-not keeps tools whose name is in active. Registry has "read", "edit", "search", "audit-log". So lead agent tools: read, search, audit-log.

sub-agent removes tools whose name is in +unshared+ = '("audit-log"). So sub-agent receives "read", "search".

Wait, but the question: what tool names does (sub-agent (make-lead-agent)) actually receive. Sorted by string<: "read" < "search". So answer: read, search.

The run confirms: "read" and "search". Let me write answer.txt.

Done. Running the constructor confirms the answer.

Trace of what happens:
- `config.lisp` sets `*flags* = '(:audit)`, so in `extension.lisp` only `audit-log` gets registered (`trace` is not).
- `make-lead-agent` loads `extension.lisp`, then filters the registry to the active set `("read" "search" "audit-log" "delegate")`. The registry at that point contains `read`, `edit`, `search`, `audit-log` — so the lead agent holds `read`, `search`, `audit-log`.
- `sub-agent` strips the unshared `"audit-log"`, leaving `read` and `search`.

Sorted ascending by `string<`, and verified with `sbcl --script check.lisp` → `ok`.
